claim: The between twin-full sibling comparison enabled a direct comparison between two types of stressors while controlling for potential familial confounders.
source: and the between twin-full sibling comparison which enabled a direct comparison between two types of stressors, that is loss of a co-twin and loss of a full sibling, while controlling for potential familial confounders (e.g., genetic background was fully controlled for monozygotic twins, and partially controlled for dizygotic twins).
evidence: Statement describing the methodological strength of the study design

claim: The study had sufficient statistical power to perform all planned subgroup analyses.
source: As the largest cohort study on co-twin loss so far, we had sufficient statistical power to perform all planned subgroup analyses.
evidence: Statement about the statistical power of the study

claim: Information bias was minimized since the registration and diagnosis of exposure and outcome was compiled prospectively and independently.
source: Information bias was minimized since the registration and diagnosis of exposure and outcome was compiled prospectively and independently.
evidence: Statement about the methodological strength regarding bias reduction

claim: The availability of rich information on sociodemographic and medical factors enabled considerations of a wide range of important confounding factors.
source: Furthermore, the availability of rich information on sociodemographic and medical factors enabled considerations of a wide range of important confounding factors.
evidence: Statement about the methodological strength regarding confounder control

claim: All individuals born in Sweden between 1932 and 2013 were identified from the Total Population Register.
source: From the Total Population Register, we identified all individuals born in Sweden between 1932 and 2013.
evidence: Statement describing the data source and study population

claim: Individuals were linked to other registers in Sweden using personal identification numbers.
source: We then linked these individuals to other registers in Sweden, including the Multi-Generation Register, the Causes of Death Register, the Swedish Twin Registry, and the National Patient Register (NPR), utilizing the personal identification numbers that are uniquely assigned to all Swedish residents.
evidence: Statement describing the data linkage methodology

claim: Twin pairs were identified as full siblings born on the same day (± 1 day) from the Multi-Generation Register.
source: From the Multi-Generation Register which includes almost complete familial link for all individuals born in Sweden since 1932, we identified all twin pairs as full siblings (i.e., with the same biological father and mother) that were born on the same day (+ / - 1 day), after excluding multiple births (more than two babies)
evidence: Statement describing the operational definition of twins

claim: Among 167,600 identified twin individuals, 6,732 experienced the loss of a co-twin due to death between 1973 and 2013.
source: As shown in Figure 1, among a total of the 167,600 identified twin individuals, 6732 experienced the loss of a co-twin due to death between 1973 and 2013
evidence: Statement describing the initial exposed cohort with reference to Figure 1

claim: Twins who lost a co-twin before age of 2 years were removed from the exposed cohort (n = 1,241).
source: To enable the establishment of attachment relationship (Howe and Ross, 1990), as well as to reduce the possibility of a co-twin loss due to poor birth condition or congenital defects that shares within a twin pair, twins who lost a co-twin before age of 2 years were removed from the exposed cohort (n = 1,241).
evidence: Statement describing an exclusion criterion with citation

claim: Twins who had a history of psychiatric disorders before the index date were excluded (n = 790).
source: We further excluded twins who had a history of psychiatric disorders (n = 790) or emigrated (n = 173) before the index date
evidence: Statement describing an exclusion criterion

claim: Twins who emigrated before the index date were excluded (n = 173).
source: We further excluded twins who had a history of psychiatric disorders (n = 790) or emigrated (n = 173) before the index date
evidence: Statement describing an exclusion criterion

claim: Per each exposed twin, five unexposed twins were randomly selected and individually matched by sex and birth year.
source: Then, per each exposed twin, we randomly selected five unexposed twins (individually matched by sex and birth year, n = 22,640) who were free of psychiatric disorders and whose co-twins were alive on the index date for exposed twins (i.e., the index date for unexposed twin).
evidence: Statement describing the matching procedure

claim: 4,939 full siblings of 2,761 twins exposed to a co-twin loss were identified through the Multi-Generation Register.
source: Through the Multi-Generation Register, we identified 4939 full siblings of 2761 twins exposed to a co-twin loss, who were alive and free of psychiatric disorders on the death date of the deceased twin (i.e., the index date for the exposed full siblings).
evidence: Statement describing the twin-sibling cohort composition

claim: Follow-up started from the index date until the occurrence of psychiatric disorders, death, emigration, or end of follow-up (December 31, 2013), whichever occurred first.
source: Follow-up of all study participants started from the index date, until the occurrence of any or a specific type of psychiatric disorders, death, emigration, or the end of follow-up (December 31, 2013), whichever occurred first.
evidence: Statement describing the follow-up procedure

claim: Information on death of a co-twin and its underlying causes was obtained from the Swedish Causes of Death Register.
source: We obtained information on death of a co-twin and its underlying causes from the Swedish Causes of Death Register, which is available electronically for register-based research since 1952.
evidence: Statement describing the data source for exposure

claim: Unnatural death was defined as a death with any external cause according to ICD codes.
source: Unnatural death was defined as a death with any external cause (according to the 8-10th Swedish revisions of the International Classification of Diseases [ICD] codes, Supplementary file 1-Table 1) as one of the documented causes based on the Causes of Death Register.
evidence: Statement describing the operational definition of unnatural death

claim: First-ever inpatient or outpatient hospital visit with a psychiatric disorder was identified from the National Patient Register.
source: Any, first-ever, inpatient or outpatient hospital visit with a psychiatric disorder as one of the registered diagnoses during the follow-up was identified from the NPR (ICD eight and ICD nine codes: 290–315, ICD 10 codes: F00-F99).
evidence: Statement describing the outcome ascertainment

claim: Information on zygosity of twins was mainly retrieved from the Swedish Twin Registry.
source: Information on zygosity of twins was mainly retrieved from the Swedish Twin Registry, and we additionally counted all twin pairs with sex discordance as dizygotic twins.
evidence: Statement describing the data source for zygosity

claim: All twin pairs with sex discordance were counted as dizygotic twins.
source: Information on zygosity of twins was mainly retrieved from the Swedish Twin Registry, and we additionally counted all twin pairs with sex discordance as dizygotic twins.
evidence: Statement describing the operational definition for dizygotic twins

claim: Data on education level, family income, and marital status at index date were acquired from the Longitudinal Integration Database for Health Insurance and Labor Market study.
source: We acquired data on education level, family income, and marital status at index date from the Longitudinal Integration Database for Health Insurance and Labor Market study.
evidence: Statement describing the data source for socioeconomic variables

claim: History of severe somatic diseases was collected from the National Patient Register.
source: History of severe somatic diseases (including myocardial infarction, congestive heart failure, cerebrovascular disease, chronic pulmonary disease, connective tissue disease, diabetes, renal diseases, liver diseases, ulcer diseases, and HIV infection/AIDS, with ICD codes listed in Supplementary file 1-Table 1) was also collected from the NPR.
evidence: Statement describing the data source for medical history

claim: Family history of psychiatric disorders was defined as any diagnosis of or death due to psychiatric disorders, suicide, or suicide attempts among first-degree relatives.
source: Family history of psychiatric disorders was defined as any diagnosis of or death due to psychiatric disorders, suicide, or suicide attempts among the first-degree relatives (i.e., biological parents and siblings) of the study participants, according to the NPR or Causes of Death Register.
evidence: Statement describing the operational definition of family history

claim: The study was approved by the Regional Ethics Review Board in Stockholm, Sweden.
source: The study was approved by the Regional Ethics Review Board in Stockholm, Sweden.
evidence: Statement about ethical approval

claim: The association between loss of a co-twin and risk of psychiatric disorders was estimated using hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals derived from conditional Cox regression models.
source: We estimated the association between loss of a co-twin and risk of psychiatric disorders using hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), derived from conditional Cox regression models.
evidence: Statement describing the statistical method

claim: Time since the index date was applied as the underlying time scale in the Cox models.
source: Time since the index date was applied as the underlying time scale.
evidence: Statement describing the time scale used in statistical analysis

claim: The proportional hazards assumption was checked graphically and by Schoenfeld's partial residuals, with no indication of violation.
source: Throughout our analyses, we checked the proportional hazards assumption graphically and by Schoenfeld's partial residuals; and neither of them revealed any indication of violation of this assumption.
evidence: Statement describing the validation of statistical assumptions
